reading.body:
Robert Garcia's AI record shows five AI-company PAC contributions in twelve months and one AI oversight measure, with no vote on that measure recorded.

The money is steady and modest: $1,000 to $2,500 per committee, from Amazon, Google, Intel, Meta, and Microsoft, between August 2025 and June 2026. The Microsoft entries on 2025-09-29 are a $2,500 contribution and a matching $2,500 refund, which nets to zero. The contributions come from corporate PACs, not the companies directly, and the data records no link between any contribution and any vote.

The legislative side is thinner than the money side. Garcia cosponsored H.Res. 286, an inquiry into DOGE's use of AI, and voted on three bills, yea twice and absent twice. The data does not say what H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, or S. 146 contain, so it cannot show whether any of them touch compute, data centers, or grid capacity.

What this record does not cover is as important as what it does. It holds only events this site has indexed, only federal filings, and only AI-labeled items, so it is not a complete campaign finance picture and not a full voting record. It establishes proximity between money and legislation, nothing more.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Robert Garcia: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 14 events.
